topic_summary: Decision menu for Spain's Article 93 Special Tax Regime (Beckham Law) — covering eligibility conditions, qualifying work reasons, tax rates, and mid-regime continuity risks. Every dish is grounded in Artículo 93 IRPF (snapshot 7f3ff874) and a verbatim competitor gap.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes your situation with respect to Spain?

options.label: I have recently moved to Spain (or am about to move) and want to understand whether I can elect the Beckham regime
I already elected the Beckham regime and want to know how long it lasts or what ends it
I am a Spanish citizen or permanent resident who has always lived in Spain
None of these / I am not sure which applies to me

questions.text: Were you a Spanish tax resident during any of the cinco períodos impositivos (five tax periods) immediately before your displacement to Spain?

options.label: No — I was not a Spanish tax resident during any of those five prior tax periods
Yes — I was a Spanish tax resident during at least one of those five prior tax periods
I am not sure whether my earlier stays in Spain counted as tax-residency periods

questions.text: What is the primary reason for your displacement to Spain? (This determines which qualifying pathway under Artículo 93 applies to you.)

options.label: I moved under an employment contract with a Spanish employer, or was ordered to relocate by my employer (not a professional sports contract)
I work remotely for a foreign company using digital/telematic means and hold (or plan to hold) a Digital Nomad Visa
I moved to become a director or administrator of a Spanish company
I moved to start or run an entrepreneurial business activity in Spain
I am a highly qualified professional carrying out an economic activity in Spain
I moved to Spain under a professional sports contract
None of these / I am not sure which category applies

questions.text: For highly qualified professionals: does your qualifying remuneration represent more than 40% of your total business, professional, and employment income combined?

options.label: Yes — my qualifying remuneration represents more than 40% of my total business, professional, and employment income
No — my qualifying remuneration represents 40% or less of that combined total
I am not sure what share of my income qualifies

questions.text: What aspect of your active Beckham regime do you want to understand?

options.label: How long the regime lasts and when it ends (including for family members)
What tax rates apply to my income under the regime
Whether a gap or interruption in my employment affects my status
What events could cause me to lose the regime
None of these / something else

terminals.heading: I may have lived in Spain before — do my prior years disqualify me?
terminals.result_copy: The Beckham regime requires that you were not a Spanish tax resident during any of the cinco períodos impositivos prior to your displacement. Whether earlier stays in Spain constituted tax-residency periods depends on facts — such as the number of days present, the location of your centre of economic interests, and your habitual residence — that only you and your adviser can verify. This dish explains the determination to make and the evidence to gather; it does not assert your outcome.

terminals.heading: I moved to Spain under an employment contract or employer-ordered transfer (not a sports contract)
terminals.result_copy: Under Artículo 93.1.b).1.º, displacement to Spain under an ordinary or special employment relationship with a Spanish employer, an employer-ordered relocation supported by a displacement letter, or remote work for a foreign employer carried out exclusively via digital/telematic means may satisfy the work-reason condition. Professional sports contracts are explicitly excluded from this pathway. If your facts match one of these three sub-cases, the work-reason condition is indicated as met — subject to all other eligibility conditions also being satisfied.

terminals.heading: I am a remote worker for a foreign company and hold (or plan to hold) a Digital Nomad Visa
terminals.result_copy: Since Ley 28/2022, remote employees of foreign companies who work exclusively via digital/telematic means may satisfy the work-reason condition under Artículo 93.1.b).1.º. Holding the international telework visa (Digital Nomad Visa) under Ley 14/2013 is explicitly listed as a qualifying circumstance. However, the visa grants residency — it does not automatically confer the tax regime. You must separately elect the regime via Modelo 149 and satisfy all other eligibility conditions.

terminals.heading: I moved to Spain to become a director or administrator of a company
terminals.result_copy: Becoming an administrator of a Spanish entity may satisfy the work-reason condition under Artículo 93.1.b).2.º. One restriction applies: if the entity is a 'patrimonial entity' as defined in Artículo 5.2 of the Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades, you must not hold a participation that makes the entity a related party under Artículo 18 of Ley 27/2014. If neither restriction applies to your situation, the work-reason condition is indicated as met — subject to all other eligibility conditions also being satisfied.

terminals.heading: I moved to Spain to start or run an entrepreneurial business activity
terminals.result_copy: Carrying out an entrepreneurial economic activity in Spain may satisfy the work-reason condition under Artículo 93.1.b).3.º, provided the activity is certified as 'actividad emprendedora' through the procedure in Artículo 70 of Ley 14/2013. The certification process is a prerequisite — without it, this qualifying reason cannot be relied upon. If certification is obtained and all other eligibility conditions are met, the work-reason condition is indicated as satisfied.

terminals.heading: I am a highly qualified professional — does the 40% income threshold apply to me?
terminals.result_copy: For highly qualified professionals carrying out an economic activity in Spain, Artículo 93 requires that qualifying remuneration represents more than 40% of the totality of business, professional, and employment income combined. If your qualifying remuneration exceeds that share, this eligibility route is indicated as potentially available — subject to all other conditions. If your qualifying remuneration represents 40% or less of that combined total, this eligibility route is not available to you under the verified rule. Review with an adviser is recommended to confirm the precise income classification.

terminals.heading: How long does the Beckham regime last once I qualify?
terminals.result_copy: The Beckham regime covers the tax period in which the change of residence occurs and the cinco períodos impositivos following it. This is the maximum statutory window; the regime ends earlier if a disqualifying event occurs. Family members who displace to Spain with the main contributor, or subsequently (provided the first tax period of the regime has not yet ended), may also be covered. This dish states the rule — whether the regime continues to apply in your specific circumstances depends on facts to be verified with an adviser.

terminals.heading: What income tax rates apply under the Beckham regime?
terminals.result_copy: Under the Beckham regime, the following rates apply as stated in the verified source: 24% on the taxable base up to 600.000 euros; 47% on the amount from 600.000,01 euros onwards. For savings income, a progressive scale applies across the brackets set out in the verified figures. The withholding rate on employment income is 24%; when retributions paid by the same payer during the natural year exceed 600.000 euros, the withholding rate applicable to the excess is 47%. These are the statutory rates; your actual liability depends on your specific income composition and must be calculated with an adviser.

terminals.heading: What happens to my Beckham status if my employment ends (redundancy, resignation, contract termination)?
terminals.result_copy: The Beckham regime may be lost before the cinco períodos impositivos window expires if a disqualifying event occurs. The conditions that can terminate the regime depend on the qualifying pathway under which you elected it and on changes in your personal or professional circumstances. This dish identifies the categories of disqualifying events described in the authority source; whether any applies to your situation requires verification with an adviser.

terminals.heading: Does maternity leave, a sabbatical, or another employment interruption affect my Beckham status?
terminals.result_copy: A gap or interruption in the employment or activity that formed the basis for your Beckham regime election may affect your continued eligibility. Whether an interruption is disqualifying depends on its nature, duration, and the qualifying pathway under which you elected the regime. This dish describes the relevant considerations from the authority source; the impact on your specific situation requires verification with an adviser.

terminals.heading: I moved to Spain under a professional sports contract — am I excluded?
terminals.result_copy: Professional sports contracts are explicitly excluded from the qualifying work-reason pathways under Artículo 93.1.b).1.º. A displacement to Spain under a professional sports contract does not satisfy the work-reason condition for the Beckham regime. This is a definite negative outcome under the verified rule: the sports-contract exclusion applies, and this eligibility route is not available.

terminals.heading: The Beckham regime may not be the question your move turns on
terminals.result_copy: The Beckham regime is a special tax treatment for people who BECOME Spanish tax residents because of a qualifying work reason — an employment contract or employer-ordered relocation, remote work for a foreign employer, a company directorship, a certified entrepreneurial activity, or highly qualified professional work. If none of those describes your move, the regime is not the right frame for your situation, and that is not the same as saying you have no Spanish tax question to answer. Retirees and people relocating on passive or investment income fall outside the regime entirely, because Article 93 targets inbound workers and their earned income. People already resident in Spain, or returning after a recent Spanish tax-residency period, run into the prior-residency condition rather than the work-reason one. In each of those cases the useful next step is ordinary Spanish residency and IRPF planning with a qualified gestor or asesor fiscal — and for a pension or investment profile, a wealth and pensions adviser rather than a Beckham specialist, because it is a different speciality.

terminals.heading: Your Beckham position needs a closer look
terminals.result_copy: Your answers do not yet establish whether the Beckham regime is available to you. Article 93 stacks several conditions and each one has to hold on its own: you must not have been a Spanish tax resident during any of the cinco períodos impositivos before your displacement; your move must be attributable to one of the qualifying work reasons; and the election itself must be made through Modelo 149 inside the statutory window. Any single one of those can decide the outcome by itself, and the two people most often get wrong are the prior-residency count — which turns on days present, the centre of your economic interests and your habitual residence, not on whether you felt settled — and the election deadline, which runs from Spanish social-security registration rather than from arrival or from your employment start date, and which is not extended by a late realisation that the regime existed. A short personalised review sets out which condition is actually in doubt for you and what evidence resolves it, while an application can still be made.
